# ClientPilot

> ClientPilot (https://clientpilot.dev) turns a freelance developer's profile into ready-to-publish client acquisition content: LinkedIn posts, cold outreach emails, a Dev.to article, freelance platform profiles, portfolio page copy and elevator pitches. Made by Dizid (https://dizid.com), Marc de Ruijter.

## What it does
- You sign in with Google and give it your portfolio URL, GitHub profile or a pasted CV; it drafts your profile (skills, stack, projects, target market) for you to check.
- One generation produces six content types from that profile: LinkedIn posts (10), outreach email templates, a Dev.to case-study article, platform profiles (Toptal, Arc.dev, freelance.nl and others), portfolio /hire page copy, and elevator pitches (30-second pitch, X bio, LinkedIn headline, GitHub README).
- Target context: describe an ideal client (startup, agency, a niche, or paste the prospect's website) and the messaging, pain points and positioning are tailored to that client. Several targets can share one profile.
- Every piece is editable inline, can be regenerated on its own, copied, and tracked as draft, used or replied.
- Content is generated with Anthropic's Claude.

## Pricing
- Free: 1 preview generation, see all content types, limited copy/export.
- Pro: $9 per month. Unlimited generations, all content types, full copy/export, weekly content refresh. Cancel anytime from Settings; refund on request within 7 days of purchase.
- Lifetime: $69 one-time payment. Everything in Pro, lifetime updates, priority support.

## Who it is for
- Freelance and indie developers who want a steady stream of client-facing content without writing it from scratch each week.
- Not an API or auto-poster yet: you copy the content and publish it yourself (LinkedIn and Dev.to publishing integrations are on the roadmap).

## Blog (guides for freelance developers)
- Index: https://clientpilot.dev/blog
- How to set your freelance developer rate (with 2026 data) (Arc, Upwork, Malt and US BLS figures with their limits; hourly vs day rate vs fixed price; floor-rate calculation incl. platform fees; raising your rate): https://clientpilot.dev/blog/freelance-developer-rates
- Freelance platform fees for developers compared (2026) (Upwork, Fiverr, Contra, Malt, Toptal, Arc, Freelancer.com, PeoplePerHour, Braintrust, Lemon.io; free channels; a 30-day plan): https://clientpilot.dev/blog/freelance-platform-fees-compared
- Cold email for freelance developers: template and rules (example email, two follow-ups, Gmail and Yahoo sender requirements, CAN-SPAM, UK PECR, GDPR and national rules): https://clientpilot.dev/blog/cold-email-freelance-developer
- LinkedIn outreach for freelance developers: a 3-step plan (profile basics, connection note vs InMail vs message, LinkedIn's own invitation limits and automation rules, three example messages): https://clientpilot.dev/blog/linkedin-outreach-freelance-developer
- Freelance follow-up emails: when, how often, templates (timing by situation, what each follow-up should add, four templates incl. a breakup email, a tracking sheet, CAN-SPAM, PECR, GDPR and Gmail/Yahoo notes): https://clientpilot.dev/blog/freelance-follow-up-email
- Freelance developer contract: the clauses that protect you (scope and exclusions, change requests, deposits and payment terms, acceptance, IP assignment on full payment under US copyright law, reuse license for your own code, open source, confidentiality, GDPR Article 28 processor terms, warranty, liability cap, termination, handover) and New York City's and New York State's written-contract rules: https://clientpilot.dev/blog/freelance-developer-contract-clauses
